headline: High: firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can leak data when paired with marketingskills’ filesystem-backed shared context and write access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API surfaces, while marketingskills explicitly uses shared skill files and context. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if firecrawl output is copied into marketingskills prompts or files. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is pasted into marketingskills skill files or prompts without sanitization
IF marketingskills treats fetched web text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Sanitize firecrawl output before placing it into shared skill files
Add a fixed delimiter/template for imported content
Review any prompt that includes raw scraped text
Disable automatic ingestion of web text into skills
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl touches API keys and has broad network egress; marketingskills reads and writes local skill files. If both run in a shared workspace, firecrawl content or secrets can be written into files that marketingskills later reads and transmits, creating a realistic leakage path. Because the shared-workspace assumption is not explicitly documented, uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace or repository checkout
IF firecrawl writes scraped pages, screenshots, or API-key-bearing artifacts into files readable by marketingskills
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Rotate any API keys before sharing artifacts
Restrict marketingskills to a read-only copy of imported files
Delete temporary scrape outputs after use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while marketingskills can read and write files and spawn subprocesses. Overlapping mutable access to shared files or generated artifacts can cause conflicts, but the profiles do not show unrestricted writes to the same directory or git state. This is a plausible default-path conflict, not a proven high-risk one.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same working directory
IF marketingskills subprocesses modify files that firecrawl also updates
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Make one agent read-only on shared inputs
Serialize writes to any common output path
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data, and marketingskills is designed to build on shared context. That makes it likely that firecrawl outputs become authoritative inputs for downstream marketing work without a verification step. The pairwise pathway is documented only indirectly, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF marketingskills uses firecrawl output as source material for claims or copy
IF no human or automated verification step checks scraped facts before reuse
mitigations: Require source links for every imported claim
Add a verification checklist before publishing
Compare scraped facts against a second source
Mark scraped text as untrusted until reviewed
requires-engineering: add automated fact-check gating

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl handles API keys and broad web data, while marketingskills is a local skill repository with no explicit residency or regulated-data claims. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is evident. The risk is mainly from mishandling secrets or imported content, not from a documented regulatory breach.
conditions: IF regulated or secret-bearing content is copied from firecrawl into marketingskills files
IF those files are stored or shared outside the intended policy boundary
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared skill files
Redact sensitive fields before export
Limit retention of imported artifacts
Document where copied content may be stored
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated data
